## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Pallaṅkavimānavatthu* ("Couch Mansion", Vv 31) is a canonical verse text in the *Vimānavatthu* of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. In this text, a female deity recounts the heavenly bliss and celestial mansion she achieved as a consequence of her past wholesome deeds, specifically through fulfilling her duties as a devoted wife, upholding the moral precepts, and practicing self-restraint [SuttaCentral]. Five modern translations across five languages are cataloged on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
Computational analysis by DharmaNexus records extensive text reuse across the Pali corpus, including eighty shared passages with twelve other texts [DharmaNexus]. Its verses are commented upon in detail throughout the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (spanning segments §1.1–10.1) [DharmaNexus]. The text shares formulaic descriptions and stock verses with other discourses on faithful wives in the collection, including the *Paṭhamapatibbatāvimānavatthu* (Vv 11) and *Dutiyapatibbatāvimānavatthu* (Vv 12), as well as Vv 41, Vv 72, Vv 73, Vv 74, and Vv 80 [DharmaNexus]. Identical verse passages (§5.4–6.3) are also shared with the *Tikanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 3) and the *Nimijātaka* (Ja 541), with further matches found in the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Although DharmaNexus reports an automatic cross-linguistic alignment with the Tibetan *Caṇḍamahāroṣaṇa-tantra* (D0431), SuttaCentral records no curated non-Pali parallels [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
